messages:
matt: quick heads-up — noticed a perf regression after we flipped the kernel-selector -> v2 on canary. short seqlen p99 jumped from ~48ms -> ~130ms. traces show lots of KV cache misses right after driver handshake changes.

maya: yikes. do we have a repro profile?

matt: yes, i ran the short-seq workload against canary 3 times, attached a tiny summary: p50 ~12ms, p95 ~34ms, p99 ~130ms. the flame shows cache miss spikes aligned with driver reconnects and a new `driver_meta` field being added to the cache key.

simon: that matches what i saw in profiling yesterday. the handshake now includes a transient `driver_session_id` which changes every reconnect — that got into the keyspace.

liz: that would totally churn keys. current key format (simplified):
```
key = f"{model_id}:{kernel_variant}:{seqlen_bin}:{driver_session_id}"
```

matt: right — and since `driver_session_id` changes on any runtime restart or handshake change, the cache never hits after a deploy or model swap.

maya: propose we do two things: 1) stop including volatile handshake tokens in primary key; 2) add a stable driver fingerprint + key version so we can rotate safely.

simon: agreed. suggested new key:
```
key_v2 = f"v2:{model_hash}:{kernel_group}:{seqlen_bin}:{driver_fingerprint}"
# driver_fingerprint = hash(driver_binary_version + config_flags)
```
This keeps keys stable across reconnects but still invalidates when driver semantics actually change.

matt: nice. what about persistence and migration? we have millions of keys in RocksDB (local cache), and a rollout would need compatibility.

maya: plan: dual-write both old and new keys for 7 days, read old-first during rollout. after 7 days switch read precedence to key_v2, then garbage-collect old keys asynchronously with a TTL sweep. also expose a migration metric `cache_dual_write_hits` to monitor.

liz: need to be careful about space blowup during dual-write. we should add a compaction schedule and a cap: if total cache size increases > 12% in 24h abort rollout. also enable prefix compaction on `v2:` namespace.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: canary 2026-02-28 14:02 UTC — p99 short-seq increased by 171% vs baseline.

matt: thanks perf-bot. simon — can you add a lightweight unit test that simulates reconnect and ensures driver_session_id doesn't cause a miss for key_v2?

simon: yep, i'll add a test in runtime/cache/tests/test_key_migration.py. test will: create entry with key_v2, simulate reconnect (new session id), ensure lookups hit same entry.

maya: i'll draft the PR for the schema change and dual-write logic. propose feature-flag `cache.key_migration_v2` default off, toggle for canary.

liz: ops checklist: 1) create monitoring dashboard (dual_write_hits, cache_size, p99_short_seq) 2) set canary threshold alerts 3) readiness to rollback (disable dual-write + delete v2 writes).

matt: rollout timeline suggestion: PR + tests today, enable feature-flag on internal canary tomorrow, monitor 48h, if stable promote to external canary and 1-week dual-write, then flip read precedence.

maya: also one more thing — kernel selection logic sometimes picks a heavier kernel for tiny sequences because of mistaken kernel_family mapping. i'll add a seqlen-bin->kernel_family map test to the same PR.

simon: good catch. kernel_family must be orthogonal to driver fingerprint decisions. otherwise key_v2 could map different kernel_family when the selector changes, producing silent mismatches. add a unit that asserts kernel_family stability across selector versions when model architecture identical.

matt: ok. owners: maya = PR + migration plan, simon = tests + kernel_family regression checks, liz = monitoring + ops rollback plan. i'll run the canary and watch perf dashboards.

maya: PR up in ~3h. leaving notes in the PR about compaction and abort thresholds. :thumbsup:

matt: awesome. thanks team.

liz: adding the alert now.

perf-bot: note: schedule perf-run `short-seq-100k` after PR merge.

matt: will do.

simon: any objections to using `v2:` namespace instead of bumping numeric version inside key? makes prefix compaction simpler.

maya: fine with `v2:` — keeps Rocks prefixes tidy.

matt: cool. closing thread — post PR link when ready and i'll attach canary results.

liz: 👍
